Construct a Separable Penalty From a Distribution

Source: R/distrib_penalty.R
distrib_penalty.Rd

Builds the penalty \(\rho(D\beta;\theta) = -\sum_i \log f(b_i;\theta)\), where \(f\) is a distributions7 density and the \(b_i\) are the successive blocks of \(D\beta\). A univariate parent gives blocks of one coordinate, which is the separable penalty; a \(p\)-variate parent gives blocks of \(p\), a prior under which the coordinates of one block depend on each other while the blocks stay independent.

Usage

distrib_penalty(d, map = NULL, n_coef = NULL, kinks = NULL)

Arguments

d

A continuous distributions7 object, univariate or multivariate; typically a distributions7::fixed() wrapper holding the location at zero. A univariate object must inherit from distributions7::continuous_distrib; otherwise the constructor signals an error that names the distribution. A multivariate object is rejected in the same way when it is, or wraps, the distributions7 multinomial; a multivariate family written outside distributions7 is not checked. An object whose dimension is neither "univariate" nor "multivariate" is rejected.

map

The matrix \(D\), with one column per coefficient, or NULL (the default) for the identity. A Matrix object keeps its storage, so a diagonal or sparse map is not densified, and a square map whose off-diagonal entries are all zero is stored as a Matrix::Diagonal().

n_coef

The number of coefficients. It is required when map is NULL and ignored otherwise, the count being ncol(map).

kinks

The points where the parent's log-density is not differentiable in its argument. With NULL, the default, they are derived by distrib_kinks() for a univariate parent and set to numeric(0) for a multivariate one, a kink being a point of a scalar argument. A numeric vector is used as given, and numeric(0) declares that there are none.

Value

A DistribPenalty() object whose hyperparameters, bounds, links and params_smooth are those of the parent distribution.

Hyperparameters and derivatives

The properties params, params_bounds, link_params and params_smooth are copied from the distribution, and every derivative is the distribution's own, carried through the map:

$$\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial\beta} = -D'\ell^{(y)}, \qquad \frac{\partial^2\rho}{\partial\beta^2} = -D'\,\mathrm{diag}(\ell^{(yy)})\,D, \qquad \frac{\partial^2\rho}{\partial\beta\,\partial\theta_k} = -D'\ell^{(y\theta_k)},$$

where the middle matrix is block diagonal instead of diagonal when the parent is multivariate. The hyperparameter derivatives are the parent's score and Hessian summed over the blocks, and the mixed derivative comes from distributions7::distrib_cross_y().

Normalizing constant and Jacobian

The normalizing constant of the density is kept, so the value is the negative log prior density. This makes a free scale or a free \(\nu\) estimable by a marginal criterion. With the constant dropped, the value of a Gaussian prior would decrease toward zero as its scale grows, and a criterion would send the scale to infinity.

Under a square nonsingular map the value also carries the Jacobian of \(\beta \mapsto D\beta\): it is \(-\sum_i \log f(b_i;\theta) - \log\lvert\det D\rvert\), the negative log-density of \(\beta\) instead of that of \(D\beta\). Under a diagonal map, which is the map that standardization builds, the term is \(\sum_j \log\lvert d_j\rvert\). The term is constant in \(\beta\) and in \(\theta\), so it changes no derivative, and it makes a marginal criterion invariant to the units of a covariate. The determinant is computed once, when the penalty is built, and stored in the log_jacobian property; for a diagonal map it is recomputed from the entries each time the value is computed. Under a map that is not square, or is singular, \(\exp(-\rho)\) does not integrate to one over \(\beta\), is_proper() returns FALSE, and the value is \(-\sum_i \log f(b_i;\theta)\) with no further constant.

A square base matrix or Matrix object whose off-diagonal entries are all exactly zero is stored as a Matrix::Diagonal() map. The proximal operator, the draws and the Jacobian recognize a diagonal map by its class, so this conversion makes their result depend on the entries of the map and not on the class in which it was supplied.

A multivariate parent

The caller centers the parent, typically through distributions7::fixed() at a zero mean, and the matrix parameter carries the dependence within a block. The number of values at which the penalty is read must divide into whole blocks; otherwise the constructor signals an error that names the block width and the count.

A blockwise penalty has no proximal operator, because that operator acts one coordinate at a time and the coordinates of a block do not separate. has_prox() returns FALSE and penalty_prox() signals an error.

See also

ridge_penalty(), lasso_penalty(), elasticnet_penalty() and heavy_penalty() for the named instances, quadratic_penalty() and structured_penalty() for the quadratic branches, distrib_kinks() for how the kinks are found, distributions7::fixed() for the wrapper that centers a parent.

Examples

# A Gaussian prior at zero: the separable form of the ridge, written by
# its standard deviation instead of a precision.
d <- distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), mu = 0)
pen <- distrib_penalty(d, n_coef = 3)
pen@params
#> [1] "sigma"
penalty_value(pen, c(1, 0, -1), list(sigma = 2))
#> [1] 5.086257

# The same number from stats::dnorm().
-sum(stats::dnorm(c(1, 0, -1), sd = 2, log = TRUE))
#> [1] 5.086257

# A correlated prior over two coefficients per block, three blocks. The
# hyperparameters are the matrix parameter's free values.
mv <- distributions7::fixed(distributions7::mvgaussian1_distrib(2),
                            mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0)
pen2 <- distrib_penalty(mv, n_coef = 6)
pen2@block
#> [1] 2
pen2@params
#> [1] "sigma_log_L1" "sigma_log_L2" "sigma_L2.1"  
penalty_value(pen2, c(1, 0, -1, 0.5, 0.2, -0.3),
              list(sigma_log_L1 = 0, sigma_log_L2 = 0, sigma_L2.1 = 0.4))
#> [1] 7.090831

# The blockwise penalty has no proximal operator.
has_prox(pen2)
#> [1] FALSE

# A count that does not divide into blocks is rejected.
try(distrib_penalty(mv, n_coef = 5))
#> Error : 'fixed multivariate gaussian [2d, sigma=log_cholesky] [mu1=0,mu2=0]' is 2-variate, so the 5 values it is read at must divide into
#>   whole blocks; 5 does not.

# A square nonsingular map adds -log|det D| to the value, and a diagonal
# base matrix is stored as a Matrix::Diagonal.
D <- matrix(c(2, 1, 0, 3), 2)
pen3 <- distrib_penalty(d, map = D)
penalty_value(pen3, c(0.4, -0.7), list(sigma = 1))
#> [1] 1.811118
-sum(stats::dnorm(D %*% c(0.4, -0.7), log = TRUE)) - log(abs(det(D)))
#> [1] 1.811118
methods::is(distrib_penalty(d, map = diag(c(2, 3)))@map, "diagonalMatrix")
#> [1] TRUE
